title: Inference for Off-Policy Value at Critical Geometric Coverage in a Run-Length Chain
banked_reason: The delivered claims are two-sided and contain no deferred conjecture, so the below-field assessment is driven by the benchmark’s exceptionally narrow scope and limited econometric significance rather than an unmatched theorem direction.
gap_reasons: The delivered claims are two-sided and contain no deferred conjecture, so the below-field assessment is driven by the benchmark's exceptionally narrow scope and limited econometric significance rather than an unmatched theorem direction.

Extend the exact risk, studentization, and honest-length results uniformly from the single calibration p=1/4, q=1/2 to a compact family of reset chains with known p and critical target q=sqrt(p), including nonstationary initial states.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the fixed-chain minimax risk, uniform studentization, conditional honest interval, matched length, and local crossover claims. The Chen–Shao Berry–Esseen citation was checked against the author-hosted primary paper and attested; the math panel passed. The field-tier review found the sound result too narrow, and a future re-raise would need the full theorem package uniformly over a compact family of reset probabilities and nonstationary starts.
tldr: A target policy can have bounded action likelihood ratios while moving stationary mass onto states that the behavior policy visits only at a critical geometric rate. In the fixed run-length experiment, an untuned occupied-cell mean estimator with midpoint imputation has a reward-table-uniform studentized Gaussian limit, while a separate observable interval covers conditionally on every supported state-action path at every sample size. The experiment yields a matching honest-length order and the exact minimax mean-squared-error constant \(1/(9\log4)\). It is also a strict subclass of the Mehrabi--Wager long-run anchor at \(C_\eta=2=\exp(\zeta_\pi)\), \(t_0=1/\log2\), and \(\zeta_\pi t_0=1\); consequently the anchor's critical logarithmic risk factor cannot generally be removed. The sharp constant, Gaussian limit, path-conditional interval, and exact local crossover curve remain benchmark-specific.
gap: MehrabiWager2024 locates the critical \(\log T/T\) risk order but leaves the equality case outside its Gaussian theorem and does not give a sharp fixed-chain constant. Independent-data weak-overlap theory does not control correlated run-length occupations, and existing long-run policy-value intervals do not give path-conditional finite-sample honesty in this experiment.
fill: The project derives exact word-overlap and reset-cycle count controls, transfers conditional independent-reward estimation through those counts, proves a uniform observable pivot and pathwise interval, and matches both interval-length order and minimax risk under the original trajectory law.
